correctness.rationale: For all j,n the corridor condition is equivalent to heights whose diameter is ≤B. Residues of these heights are −kα mod 1, dense by irrationality, proving no points for B<1. At B=1 interval counts are only floor(nα) or ceil(nα), hence the classical Sturmian characterization gives the exact minimal zero-entropy shift. For B>1, exchanges at disjoint 01 sites selected by a rotation interval of length ε modify only one height each, raising it from (θ−1,θ] into (θ,θ+ε), so every subset gives globally valid corridors B>1+ε. Weyl equidistribution yields εn+o(n) choices and entropy ≥ε log2; taking ε to the endpoint gives the bound. Uniform frequency α excludes periodic points; positive entropy vs embedded Sturmian zero entropy excludes minimality. Every inference covers all irrational slopes and all index positions. A separately executed finite checker passed six families; it is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical uniform discrepancy corridor around an irrational line gives a natural one-parameter enlargement of the Sturmian shift. The theorem pins down the exact emptiness/minimality/entropy transition at the smallest possible width, demonstrates that an arbitrarily small positive corridor excess supports exponentially many independently choosable local moves at every irrational slope, and provides an explicit slope-and-width dependent entropy lower bound. This is not merely a restatement of the known one-balanced Sturmian endpoint or aggregate integer-balance enumeration; fixed-slope quantification and arbitrarily small excess are essential. Infinite-window verification is mathematical, and the finite checks do not confer value independently.
